units.title: Forecast: rain continuing, heavier this afternoon
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Rain continues today, with a brief lull this morning before heavier and more persistent rain arrives from the south this afternoon. A further 20 to 35 mm is likely, locally 50 mm over the Brackwater hills, on already saturated ground. Wind southeasterly 3 to 4. Maximum 9 C. Tonight: rain, easing a little after midnight. Outlook: rain clearing slowly from the west late tomorrow, then drier and colder.

units.title: Service update: normal timetable
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. All sailings are operating to the normal timetable today. The restriction on vehicles over 3.5 tonnes at Gilliver has been lifted after the linkspan drains were cleared overnight. Passengers should allow extra time to reach Port Ammet terminal because of surface water on the approach road. Night crossings continue with the additional deck lighting.

units.title: Restored: Gilliver coastal feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Supply has been restored to all customers on the Gilliver coastal feeder following a short interruption at 01:48. Our insulator replacement programme on the exposed coastal spans is now substantially complete, with the final strings to be fitted today under live working. We do not expect further interruptions from this cause. Thank you for your patience over a difficult fortnight.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Lisle buoy relit
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Further to yesterday's notice, the Lisle approach west cardinal buoy has been relit and is now showing its correct characteristic. Notice cancelled. Mariners are reminded that visibility will be poor in heavy rain this afternoon and tonight, and that small boats should carry a working light after dark at all times.

units.title: Flooding: Mill Lane closed, sandbags available
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Mill Lane in Tollinby is closed between the Mill Bridge and Church Street because of flooding. Diversions are signed. The Brackwater dip on the A-road is open to one lane with pumping in progress. Sandbags remain available at the Tollinby depot from 08:00 to 16:00 today, and a second collection point is open at Brackwater village hall from noon.

units.title: Flood alert: Brackwater Burn
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound Met Office, with the river authority. A flood alert is in force for the Brackwater Burn from the reservoir overflow down to the Brackwater road bridge. River levels are rising after prolonged rain and are expected to peak this evening. Flooding of low-lying fields, footpaths and the lower car park at the village hall is possible. Avoid walking near the burn and do not cross flooded footbridges.

units.title: Waste collections: catch-up update
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Catch-up recycling rounds in Port Ammet, including Rope Walk and Chandler Street, were completed this morning. The Gilliver front will be collected tomorrow. If your box has been returned to the wrong address, please swap it with your neighbour. Residents are thanked for their patience during recent disruption.

units.title: Tides and coastal outlook
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound tides. High water Port Ammet 06:20 and 18:41; Gilliver 06:36 and 18:57. Tidal range increasing towards springs later this week. With heavy rain, surface water may collect on low quays around this evening's high tide. Sea state slight in the Sound. Visibility poor in rain, locally 2 km or less.

units.title: Goodwill payments: scheme updated
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Following feedback from customers on the Gilliver coastal feeder, we have reviewed our goodwill payment scheme. Customers who experienced interruptions totalling eight hours or more over the past fortnight, rather than twelve, can now claim a payment towards spoiled food. You do not need receipts. Claims can be made online or by phone until the end of next month.

units.title: Debris in river mouths after heavy rain
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. After prolonged heavy rain, floating debris is likely near river and burn mouths, particularly around Port Ammet harbour entrance and the Brackwater Burn outfall. Debris reported so far includes branches, fence posts and a wooden pallet. Small craft should keep a good lookout, reduce speed in poor visibility and report any large hazard on the usual channel.

units.title: Planning: weekly list of applications
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council, planning applications received this week. Lisle: single-storey rear extension, 4 Shore Terrace. Tollinby: change of use from shop to café, 11 Market Street. Port Ammet: replacement windows, Harbour Mews (conservation area). Gilliver: replacement chandlery signage, the harbour front. Brackwater: agricultural building, Upper Holly Farm. Comments may be made online for 21 days.

units.title: 18:20 departure delayed
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. The 18:20 from Port Ammet to Lisle and Gilliver will depart approximately twenty minutes late tonight because of slow loading in heavy rain. Later sailings are expected to run to time. We apologise for the delay. Passengers waiting at Lisle and Gilliver can use the covered shelters; please don't wait on the slipways.

units.title: Network status: all customers on supply
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, evening status. All customers across the Marrow Sound network are on supply. The final insulator strings on the Gilliver coastal feeder were fitted this afternoon. Crews remain on normal standby tonight. If you lose supply, please report it by phone. Thank you again to customers in Gilliver for their patience.

units.title: Evening update: last of the rain tomorrow
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound Met Office, 20:00 update. Rain totals today: Brackwater 33 mm, Carrow Point 22 mm, Port Ammet 19 mm, making around 70 mm in two days over the hills. The Brackwater Burn flood alert remains in force overnight. Rain tomorrow morning, easing through the afternoon, with clearer skies from the west in the evening and a colder night to follow.

units.title: Power back on Gilliver line after eight nights of cuts
units.author: courier
units.text: Electricity supply on the Gilliver coastal feeder has been restored after eight consecutive nights of interruptions, Sound Power Co-op said this morning. The company said its programme of insulator replacement on exposed spans near the coast was 'substantially complete' and that it did not expect further faults from the same cause. The last interruption was recorded at 01:48.

units.author: courier
units.text: The company has blamed the faults throughout on salt-fog corrosion, the build-up of salt on insulators exposed to sea air. Questions were raised this week about why interruptions continued on nights with heavy rain and no fog. A spokesperson said damage from earlier fog 'remains on the insulator until it is replaced' and that the pattern was consistent with weakened equipment failing under load.

units.author: courier
units.text: Linemen worked through the night on several occasions, including during this week's heavy rain. One Gilliver resident said she had seen 'a torch going along the poles at four in the morning, in weather I wouldn't put a dog out in'. The Co-op said it was grateful to its field staff and that no one had been injured during the work.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power also announced that it would lower the threshold for its goodwill payment scheme from twelve to eight hours of total interruption, after complaints that frequent short cuts had excluded most affected households. The chandlery on Gilliver harbour, which lost bait stock on three nights, said it would apply.

units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver's shore lighting, which failed briefly on several nights, has been on continuously since the early hours. The harbourmaster said the new permanent lighting on the slipway, funded by Sound Lines, had come through the outages 'without a flicker' because the ferry company had paid for a battery backup.

units.title: Letters: the island, the lights and the crew
units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, I have lived on the Gilliver front for forty years and never once thought about the Holm until this month. Now I look at it every evening. I don't know what the owners want with it, and I don't much care. I would like to know that the people working out there are being looked after, and I would like somebody from the company to say so in plain words. Name and address supplied, Gilliver.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, your coverage of the Kittering Holm clearance has been measured, and I thank you for it. But I am weary of correspondents and internet forums imagining sinister purposes for a perfectly lawful piece of land management. Islands are bought and sold. Trees are felled. A company which says little is not a company with something to hide. Retired surveyor, Port Ammet.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, may I make a practical suggestion? The Lisle Women's Institute used to send winter parcels to the lighthouse keepers at Carrow Point, and a similar gesture to the crew on the Holm would cost little. If Grieve Land Services would let us know where to send such things, I am sure the villages would oblige. Former headteacher, Lisle.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, the power cuts in Gilliver have been blamed on salt fog on nights when there was no fog. I am not an engineer, but I can read a weather report. I do not suggest anything mysterious. I suggest only that Sound Power tell us what actually happened, once they know, rather than what they assumed in the first week. Name supplied, Brackwater.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sir, my bins have been missed three times this month, the reason given each time being power interruptions, though the lorry runs on diesel. I note that the council has found time to publish two notices about the Holm and none about my bins. I do not require a reply. I require a collection. Retired postman, Rope Walk.

units.title: Comment: the thirty-day clearance and what it asks of crews
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Short, intense clearance contracts have become more common as landowners look for speed and certainty of cost. The Kittering Holm job, at a flat rate per tree and a day rate per worker over thirty days, is an extreme example: a fixed deadline, a remote site, the shortest days of the year and no option to extend that anyone outside the contract knows of.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contractors say the model rewards crews who keep their nerve and their kit in good order, and punishes everyone else. 'You can't make up a lost week at the end,' one site lead told the Journal. 'And on an island you can't send a man home and get another on the next bus. The crew you land with is the crew you finish with.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Health and safety advisers warn that long days in poor light raise the risk of chainsaw injuries and of fatigue-related mistakes. Several larger firms have moved away from per-tree pay on remote sites for exactly that reason. Grieve Land Services has used per-tree rates on island and upland contracts for more than a decade, according to former employees.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Whatever the merits, the model is unlikely to disappear. Landowners like a number they can budget for, and crews like a rate they can beat. The Journal would welcome letters from site leads and fellers about how short contracts work in practice, particularly on remote sites. Anonymity will be respected.

units.title: Canal basin residents move cars as water rises
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of streets around Weyhaven's old canal basin moved cars out of basement garages overnight as water rose in the basin after two days of heavy rain. The city council said the sluice at the basin's sea end had been opened to let water away at low tide, and that levels were expected to fall by tomorrow afternoon.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The docks underpass reopened yesterday evening after a second pump cleared it. Bus services through the city centre ran to time this morning, though the operator said several night buses had been diverted around Hollin Road because of standing water. Cleaners at the main bus depot spent much of the night mopping out flooded inspection pits.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Forecasters expect the rain to clear from the west late tomorrow, followed by a colder spell. The city's winter shelter at the Westgate hall will open from tomorrow night, a week earlier than planned, because of the forecast. Volunteers are asked to contact the hall directly.

units.title: Sound Lines: extra night lighting to stay
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines has confirmed that the additional deck and slipway lighting introduced when night crossings resumed last week will become permanent. The ferry operator said the lighting had been fitted following a 'crew welfare review' and had been well received by staff and passengers. It declined to say what the review had found.

units.author: courier
units.text: Night crossings were cut back for several days earlier this month after crew members reported seeing a person standing at the end of the Gilliver slipway in fog, and a separate report from the Lisle slip. The harbourmaster at Gilliver issued a notice reminding the public that slipways are closed after dark. Nobody was found on either occasion.

units.author: courier
units.text: The new slipway lighting at Gilliver has a battery backup and stayed on during recent power interruptions. The ferry's own floodlights run from the vessel's generator. 'Crews like to be able to see where they're putting the boat,' a Sound Lines spokesman said. 'That's all there is to it.'

units.title: Brackwater Burn rises: village hall opens to help
units.author: courier
units.text: Brackwater village hall opened as a collection point for sandbags this afternoon as the Brackwater Burn rose towards the top of its banks below the reservoir. The Met Office issued a flood alert for the burn from the reservoir overflow to the road bridge, with levels expected to peak this evening. No homes had flooded by late afternoon.

units.author: courier
units.text: The water company said the reservoir's overflow was working as designed, and that the higher flow in the burn was 'what the overflow is for'. The footpath along the outflow below the sluice remains closed. Two footbridges on the Brackwater Woods trail have been taped off after water was seen running over their decks.

units.author: courier
units.text: Volunteers at the hall served tea to people filling sandbags. 'We haven't had the burn this high since the winter the old bridge went,' said one long-time resident. The estate's ranger asked visitors to keep away from the woods until the water drops, and reminded the public that the reservoir car park now closes at dusk.

units.author: courier
units.text: The A-road at the Brackwater dip remains reduced to one lane. Council highways staff said the road would stay under traffic lights until pumping was complete, probably tomorrow afternoon. The Tollinby school bus will continue to use the ridge road for the rest of the week.

units.title: Rain, day two: live updates
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:25 ST. Good morning. Sound Power says all customers on the Gilliver feeder are back on supply after a short cut at 01:48, and it expects no further interruptions now that insulator work is nearly finished. More rain is on the way this afternoon, and the Met Office has issued a flood alert for the Brackwater Burn.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 10:35 ST. Mill Lane in Tollinby is now closed by flooding between the Mill Bridge and Church Street, with diversions signed. The A-road at the Brackwater dip is open to one lane. Ferries are running normally and the lorry restriction at Gilliver has been lifted.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:40 ST. Sound Power has lowered the threshold for its goodwill payments for spoiled food from twelve hours of interruption to eight. Listeners in Gilliver have been texting in all morning; one says the bait freezer at the chandlery is 'back to its usual grumbling'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 16:15 ST. Heavy rain has arrived over the Brackwater hills. Sandbags are available at Brackwater village hall as well as the Tollinby depot. The estate asks people to keep away from the reservoir woods, where two footbridges have been closed.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:05 ST. Sound Lines says the 18:20 from Port Ammet will leave about twenty minutes late because of slow loading in the rain. Sound Power's evening status: all customers on the network are on supply.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:25 ST. The Brackwater Burn is close to the top of its banks at the road bridge, but the river authority says it expects the peak within the next two hours. Residents in Brackwater have been moving cars off the lower lane. No properties have been flooded.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:20 ST. The Brackwater Burn has peaked just below the road bridge deck and is now falling slowly. The flood alert stays in force overnight. That's the last update from the news desk tonight; the overnight show takes over with your calls.

units.title: Contractor documents: availability
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Notice reference GLS-DOC-11. Contractor tax and earnings documents for the current year will be available in the contractor portal at contract close. Contractors are reminded to keep their own records of crew payments for the full period. Paper copies are available on request from the payroll office. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Boat today
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the supply boat is going out at noon as planned. The skipper says the swell's fine and the rain won't stop him. If there's anything you need on the next run that isn't on the usual list, could you let the skipper know by hand when he lands? I've also asked him to bring back any empty fuel drums so they're not left for the last day. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: The long nights are here! Lanterns from 15% off
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello again from Camp Supply! Days are short and nights are long, but our lanterns are the brightest in the Sound! Our Long Nights collection is now 15% off: rechargeable lanterns with a 40-hour run time, spare batteries in handy packs, and our much-loved string lights for cosy camps! Customer favourite: the TrailGlow 900, which one reviewer says 'lights up the whole clearing'. Stay bright! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Demob checklist
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the yard has sent their usual checklist for the end of a job, so here it is in short. 1. Fuel: any full drums stay on site for collection; empties back on the boat. 2. Saws and chains: clean, drained, cased. 3. Anything hired: a list with serial numbers, please. 4. Camp: please leave the camper and huts as you found them, the client's agent will walk round after handover. No need to reply. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: The truck
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a practical one. As the truck on the island is yours rather than Grieve's, getting it off at the end is your arrangement, not the yard's. The crew boat can't take it. If you'd like, I can pass you the number of the landing craft operator we've used before; he needs about a week's notice and good weather. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew list for pick-up
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, for the pick-up I'll use the crew list as it stands now, so whoever has gone home won't be on it and the boat will plan seats accordingly. Payroll has processed the leaver on their side. I know a crew member leaving partway through makes the last week harder. If you need anything to make up for it, tell me and I'll see what can be done. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A list going round
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. You may or may not have seen that a list of Ardent Vale's supposed other properties is circulating online this afternoon. I'm not going to report it as it stands, because parts of it don't check out. But I would like to ask, in confidence and only if you know: 1. Has Grieve worked for Ardent Vale anywhere else? 2. Have you been told anything about the company's other sites? I've put the same questions to Grieve. Kind regards, Nell Ashdown

units.title: A request from the client
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the client has asked, via their agent, that no photographs of the site are shared publicly during or after the work, and that the crew don't post about the job online. I've said that's our standard policy anyway, which it is. Could you mention it to the crew without making a fuss of it? They're very hands-off as clients go, but they're particular about this. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the skipper's back in Gilliver and says the drop went fine and the empties are aboard. He says the landing was 'a mud bath but fine'. Next run as normal. I've got the end-of-day count request from the client set up, so you'll see a short note from me most evenings now. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: A short follow-up, partly so you know I'm not chasing a story that isn't there. The seabird trust has confirmed it bought one of the listed sites at auction last spring, and the registry has no record of the reference numbers on the list. So the list is at least partly wrong. I'm still interested in whether the company owns anything else, but I wanted to be straight with you about where things stand. Nell

units.title: From Gilliver, with no questions attached
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello, this one isn't for a story. Several people in Gilliver and Lisle, including a class of schoolchildren in Tollinby, have asked me how they might send cards or small parcels to the crew. I've told them I don't know, and that I'd ask. If there is an address the company is happy to share, I'd pass it on and keep it out of the paper. No reply needed if not. Kind regards, Nell

units.title: the play video, finally
units.author: sam
units.text: hi. the school finally sent the video of the play, so I've watched the kid be a cloud seven times now. they wave their arms on the wrong beat and look extremely proud about it. mum says the dog has learned to open the kitchen bin with his nose, which is a disaster, and that she can now do the stairs 'like a mountain goat', which is a lie. I'll save the video for when you're home. love, S x

units.title: Re: your question about the Corran job
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Got your note about the Corran job and I've been sitting on it a couple of days, sorry. Honestly? Forget I said anything. I was three pints in when I sent that, and Corran was a long time ago, and half of what people say about it is pub talk anyway. Grieve pays late but pays. That's the whole story. Finish the job, get on the boat, buy me a drink. Hal

units.title: Important safety bulletin
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief, important safety bulletin from the road crew. What did the tree say when the lumberjack turned up? Nothing, it was stumped. What did the second tree say? Leaf me alone. I'll be here all week. Rained off today so I've had nothing to do but think these up. Mind your feet in the mud out there. Hal

units.title: The canal is up
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry, it's me again. Could you tell Tomas that the canal is up by our flat but we're fine, we moved the car to the hill like the man on the radio said? And that the dentist closed early so I made his soup recipe and it was not as good as his. Please don't tell him that part. Is he sleeping? Thank you for putting up with me. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: me again. the sound board has a thread where people in gilliver are talking about sending cards to 'the crew on the island' and somebody's kid has made glitter trees. I sat and cried a bit at that, which is silly. and somebody posted a list of the owners' other properties, a fort and a rock and I don't know what, and then everyone said the list was fake. I don't know what to believe. are they treating you all right? love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: sorry, last one tonight. I know you can't really email from out there, or you'd have said. I just like to think these arrive somewhere warm and you read them with a cup of tea. four more days, isn't it? mum's already planning a roast. she says she'll do the potatoes sitting down. anyway. go to sleep, whoever's reading this. love, S x

units.title: The lights tonight (sorry)
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Hello. Sorry, it's Morrow again. I said I'd stop, and I've mostly stopped. I just wanted to say the camp lights were on through the rain tonight, two of them, from my window on the front. Maud next door had her lamp on as well. I don't really know why I'm telling you, except that it seemed like the sort of thing someone on an island might want to know. You don't need to reply. I know you can't.

units.title: Is Tomas all right?
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry, one more. Someone at work said they'd heard one of the crew on the island had gone home early. I'm sure it isn't Tomas, because he would have rung me from the ferry, he always rings from the ferry. But is he all right? Is he still with you? I'm sorry to ask like this. I just wanted to hear it from someone. Ana

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: One more thing and then I'll leave you alone. People on the Sound Board were saying tonight that the property list was made up, at least partly. I thought that too. I might be wrong, but I think whatever the company wants with the island, the list won't tell you. I hope the last few days are quiet ones. Sorry again for writing so late.

units.title: Arnell field notebook: Kittering Holm, seventh day
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Seventh day. Fair, cold. Searched the north shore for the otter Jory insists lives there; found spraints, so the boatman is vindicated in one particular at least. Rabbits absent, which is odd. Mice in the camp ruins. No deer, eighth transect, and I now record it as a finding rather than a failure. [Sketch: the old timber camp clearing, three hut bases, a ring of stones the size of a cartwheel.] Jory asked again that we be off by four.

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: December 1894, continued
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 11th. Hard frost. Tally 88, the best of the month, the men in good heart and the far lines nearly cleared. Paid Rowe for a lost axe, deducted 2s. The boat brought lamp oil, 6 gall., and flour. Mr Coad asks that I keep the lamps account separate henceforth, the oil going faster than reckoned. Lamps lit 3.20. All in by the lamps.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 13th. Wind NE, sleet. No felling. Men at the saw-pit and mending. Oil account: 2 gall. since Tuesday, the lamps being kept up all night by the men's wish, two men sitting up by turns. I have entered it as Mr Coad directs. Hosken and Pascoe asked for their time and are paid off to go on Friday's boat. Roster 17. A quiet night.

units.title: Carrow Point logbook: February (excerpt)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Feb. 2nd. 00:00 Light exhibited, burning well. Wind N 2, clear, frost. 01:00 Lamp trimmed. 02:00 Clear. Remarks: Asst. Keeper Moyle requests that his application for transfer to a rock station be forwarded to the Board. Forwarded with my recommendation; he is a good keeper and a steady man. No reason given and none asked. 03:00 Clear. 04:00 Light burning well.

units.title: Lights Board survey, 1953: Kittering Holm relay (section 4)
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 4. Staffing. A relay station on the Holm ridge would require two attendants resident year-round, with relief by boat fortnightly. The survey party consisted of the undersigned, one assistant and two labourers, engaged for nine days. On each day the labourers asked to be taken off the island before dusk, and the boatman would not wait beyond four o'clock. The party accordingly worked short days. This has been allowed for in the cost estimate at section 5.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 4.1. Local enquiry in Gilliver produced no candidate willing to take the attendant posts, at the Board's standard rate or at a premium of one third. Enquiry in Port Ammet produced two candidates, both of whom withdrew after a visit. It is the undersigned's view that recruitment would be a continuing difficulty. This consideration, rather than any technical one, informs the recommendation at section 6.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 11, side B
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewee: Mr J. T., born 1899, retired boatman. Q: Did you ever take people out to the Holm? A: Plenty. Survey men, the bird lady, the timber buyers once. Q: Did anyone stay overnight? A: Not with me. Q: Why not? A: Because I'd not wait. [pause] Not for anything. You'd want your tea, wouldn't you. Q: Is that the only reason? A: That's the reason I give.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: Your sister says the lamp in the window is for the drowned. A: My sister says a lot. It's for the boats. Q: She says your mother told her that. A: Our mother told us different things, depending which of us was frightened. [laughs] I'll tell you what it's for. It's so they know the house is awake. That's what my mother said to me. Q: Who's 'they'? A: Whoever's out.

units.title: Window lamp (Gilliver custom): meanings recorded
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The meaning of the custom is recorded inconsistently. The 1976 oral history transcripts give at least four: a guide for boats; a courtesy to travellers on the shore road; a remembrance of the drowned; and, most often, a sign 'so they know the house is awake', with 'they' left undefined. The earliest written mention is a Courier column of the 1890s (Society holdings, CA 3). [citation needed: any record before 1880]

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk: 'they' is undefined because the interviewees were being coy with a young interviewer who wanted a ghost story, and gave one. Lamps in windows are a coastal courtesy recorded all over the north. I'd cut the list of meanings to the boats and the travellers, which are attested, and move the rest to a note. I accept the lamp itself is real.

units.title: 'From Our Gilliver Correspondent': on the window lamps
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: [Editor's note, G. Faulds: from the column of 2 February 1895, page 6. Note that the correspondent dates the timber men's return to 'before Christmas' here, contradicting his own column of 19 January.] Visitors to our village remark upon the lamps which burn in so many front windows through the winter nights. It is an old custom of the place, and a kindly one. Our oldest inhabitants say only that it is 'manners'. Since the timber men came home before Christmas, there are more lamps than ever.

units.title: Courier, 1954: relay station plan 'not proceeding'
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: [Editor's note: a single paragraph from page 9, 11 March 1954, beneath an advertisement for seed potatoes. The paper did not follow it up.] The Lights Board has informed the council that it will not proceed with the proposed relay station on Kittering Holm. A Board spokesman said the decision followed 'a review of staffing and running costs' and that the existing lights at Carrow Point and Lisle would continue to serve the approaches.

units.title: LB-R014: Reference, rain on cast iron (hydrophone)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LB-R014 (reference shelf). Date: day 26. Location: Gilliver, domestic water butt under a cast-iron downpipe. Kit: home-made hydrophone. Duration: 00:40:00. Content: discrete percussive events (drips), each followed by a metallic ring near 1.2 kHz and a low gurgle. Curator's note: added to the reference shelf for comparison with field recordings containing unattributed percussive events. It is not offered as an explanation of any of them.

units.title: Rendle diary: December 1936 (transcribed)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Dec 4 1936. Fine. Out at 5 with Jack, he come this time. Pots on the Holm side full, best this year. Jack would not go in past the point though, said we had plenty. Sold at the quay 2s a dozen. Mother had her lamp lit before we was up the hill. She said she always knows when we are late. Bought her a quarter of tea.

units.title: Chandlery this week
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: chandlery open 7 till 6 all week. new creels arrived on the boat yesterday, the heavy ones with the extra weight. rain gear ten percent off for anyone who's lost theirs to the weather this month, which is most of you lads. bait freezer is back to full and so is my patience

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: So there is a fridge on that floor after all. I said there'd be a simple answer and here it is, in a bin store, with a plug taped to it. I'll accept apologies from the upper floors in writing. And if the council collected bulky items when they said they would, it wouldn't still be there.

units.title: Truck stop coffee ratings, prairie edition
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: By popular request (one person, it was Jo). Coffee ratings for the eastbound run. Mile 88: burnt but hot, four out of ten. Mile 140: tastes like the pot's been on since the last election, two. Mile 212 lit stop: terrible, but the girl behind the counter tops you up without asking, seven. Home: my wife's, ten, obviously, in case she reads this.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Thank you for your service, Merle. Kennel coffee for comparison: the jar of instant in the staff room that nobody owns, which has set into a single brown rock. I chip at it with a spoon at three in the morning while Pepper watches. One out of ten, but Pepper's company makes it a five.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Any chance you'll get the orange oilskins back in, Rook? Our new deckhand has gone through his first set in a fortnight on the stern rail, and the company ones are the colour of a dead seal. Also two of those head torches with the red light setting, if you have them, for the engine room.

units.title: Brackwater Burn: is the road bridge open?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Quick one. My mum's in Brackwater and I'm meant to be taking her shopping round tonight. Is the road bridge over the burn still open, or is it closed with the flood alert? The council page says 'alert' but not whether you can drive over it. I'd rather not find out by floating.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Both of my crew are reliable witnesses and I'd stake my ticket on either of them. Two people can see two different things on two different nights in two different kinds of weather, and both be telling it straight. That's all I'll add. Logged it at the time, and I'm not going to re-log it now.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: A small piece of news, which I offer for what it is worth. I telephoned the landline number on the old catalogue submission form our young man filled in last year. A lady answered and said he 'wasn't there at present' and that she would 'tell him people had rung'. She did not sound worried. I took that as more than nothing. Regards, Ned

units.title: Group session files: catalogue status
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue note for those who took part in the Brackwater group session. Files LB-2601 to LB-2612 are now catalogued with their metadata. LB-2611, position 2 on the final night, remains marked incomplete; I've not changed its description and won't unless the recordist asks me to. Thank you all for the careful clock sync notes this time.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Thank you for your care with the catalogue, as always. When I began recording, nobody wrote anything down at all, and we have lost whole winters of tape because of it. I'm glad the young people keep proper notes. I shall be sending you two more reels from the dam works, labelled this time. Regards, Ned

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Came over the Brackwater bridge at six with the van. Open, both lanes, water about a foot below the deck and very brown and very loud. Council van parked at the end with a man watching it. Mill Lane is shut in Tollinby so go round by Church Street. You'll be fine, just don't stop on the bridge to look.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: The river authority's gauge at the bridge was at 2.31 m at 20:00 and rising slowly; the deck is at roughly 2.9. They expect the peak in the next couple of hours. Rain is easing to lighter stuff here at the point. Shopping run should be fine, but go now rather than later.
